questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a pair of micronutrients?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **Calcium and fats**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**__Concept:__

__
 
• Nutrients are the substances that are required by the organism/ plant to survive, grow, and reproduce.
 
• In the case of plants, different nutrients are absorbed by the roots and are then transported to the rest of the plant body.
 
• Xylem helps in the transportation of water, minerals, and nutrients in plants.

Explanation:__

An element is regarded as essential for a plant based on the following criteria:

 
• An element should be essential for the normal growth and reproduction of the plant.
 
• A requirement of an element should be such that it cannot be replaced by any other element.
 
• The element should be directly involved in the metabolism of the plant.

Based on the above-mentioned criteria and the quantitative requirements, nutrients are classified into two groups: Macronutrients and Micronutrients

Macronutrients:

 
• Macronutrients are needed in larger amounts by the plant tissues for their survival, growth, and other essential functions.
 
• Carbon (C), hydrogen (H), oxygen (O), nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), sulfur (S), potassium (K), calcium (Ca), and magnesium (Mg) are the macronutrients required by plants.

Micronutrients:

 
• Micronutrients are needed in smaller amounts by the plant tissues.
 
• Micronutrients required by plants are iron (Fe), manganese (Mn), copper (Cu), molybdenum (Mo), zinc (Zn), boron (B), chlorine (Cl), and nickel (Ni).
 
• Apart from these essential elements mentioned above, elements such as sodium (Na), silicon (Si), cobalt (Co), and selenium (Se) are also required by some higher plants.

questions.question: Which of the following types of plant is a seed bearing plant?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Gymnosperm__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The gymnosperms (Gymnos: naked, Sperma: seeds) are planted in which the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed, both before and after fertilization.
 
• Gymnosperms include medium-sized trees or tall trees and shrubs.
 
• Gymnosperms are mainly classified into two groups:
 
 
• Cycadophyta (Lower gymnosperm)
 
• Coniferophyta (Higher gymnosperm) 
 
 
 
• Cycas, Pinus and Ginkgo are examples of Gymnosperm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Thallophyta

 
 
• Kingdom Plantae is divided into five groups- Algae, Bryophyta, Pteridophyta, Gymnosperm, and Angiosperm.
 
• Algae
 
 
• The plant body is not differentiated from roots, stems, and leaves.
 
• They are also known as Thallophyta.
 
 
 
 
 
• Bryophyta
 
 
• These are small terrestrial plants.
 
• They show differentiation in the body design, with stem, leaf-like structures, and root-like structures.
 
 
 
• Pteridophyta
 
 
• The plant body is differentiated into roots, stems, and leaves, apart from having a specialized tissue for conduction.
 
 
 
• Gymnosperms
 
 
• Gymnosperms are plants with naked seeds.
 
 
 
• Angiosperms
 
 
• Angiosperms are seed-bearing plants. Seeds develop inside tissues that get modified to form the fruit of the plant.

questions.question: Which among the following are called the amphibians of the plant kingdom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bryophyte.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bryophyte** are also known as **amphibians** of the **plant kingdom** because they can survive on** both land and water.**
 
• Bryophytes are **non-vascular plants** that lack true roots, stems, and leaves.
 
• They reproduce through **spores **and are found in **damp and shady places.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thallophytes** are a group of plants that include **algae, fungi, and lichens.**

 
 
• They **lack differentiated tissues and organs** and are found in diverse habitats.
 
 
 
• **Angiosperms **are **flowering plants** that have seeds enclosed in a fruit.
 
 
• They are the most diverse and widespread group of plants and include **trees, shrubs, herbs, and grasses.**
 
 
 
• **Gymnosperms **are **non-flowering plants** that have seeds not enclosed in a fruit.
 
 
• They include **conifers, cycads, and ginkgo** trees and are mostly found in cold and dry regions.

questions.question: The innermost part of a flower is called the __________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**pistil.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pistil:-**

 
 
• The innermost part of a flower is called the pistil, which is the female reproductive organ of the flower.
 
• The pistil is made up of three parts: the stigma, the style, and the ovary.
 
• The stigma is the sticky tip of the pistil where pollen grains land and begin to grow.
 
• The style is the slender tube that connects the stigma to the ovary.
 
• The ovary contains the ovules, which are the eggs that, when fertilized by pollen, develop into seeds.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7238912662fe6f931b9b241c775cd6ae485aa258a7ac4d88d6edbf8ed1c5bce2.png] 

 ** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Stamens:-**

 
 
• These are the male reproductive organs of a flower and are located around the pistil.
 
• They consist of the anther, which produces pollen, and the filament, which supports the anther.
 
 
 
• **Petals:-**
 
 
• These are the colorful, often fragrant, parts of a flower that attract pollinators.
 
 
 
• **Sepals**:-
 
 
• These are the outermost parts of a flower and protect the developing bud.
 
• They are usually green and leaf-like in appearance.

questions.question: Which of the following is a part of a leaf?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Petiole.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Leaves are the parts of a plant that absorb sunlight which is vital for the process of photosynthesis.
 
• 
 
Leaves have two main parts: The leaf blade and the Stalk or the petiole

 
 
• 
 
The leaf blade__: It is also called the lamina and is usually broad and flat. It is in this layer that photosynthesis occurs.

 
 
• 
 
It contains a prominent midrib at the center of the leaf blade which is the main vein. From this midrib arise branches called veins.

 
 
• 
 
They are of different types depending upon the type of edges, the pattern of the veins, and the number of blades per leaf.

 
 
• 
 
 __The Petiole__: It is the stalk-like structure in the leaf that forms the link between the leaf blade to the stem. It has tiny tubes, that connect the veins on the leaf blade to the stem. Some of these veins facilitate the transport of water to the leaf while other one carries the food away from the leaf to other parts of the plant.

 
 
• 
 
Some plants also contain another part called__ Stipules __which are small flap-like structures that grow at the base of the petioles in order to protect the petioles when they are growing. 

 

The figure shows the parts of the leaf.

questions.question: A group of natural substances with variable phenolic structures, which are found in fruits, vegetables, and grains is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Flavonoids**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Flavonoids are a diverse group of phytonutrients found in almost all fruits and vegetables.
 
• These compounds are known for their antioxidant properties and play a crucial role in protecting the body against various diseases.
 
• Flavonoids are responsible for the vibrant colors of many fruits and vegetables.
 
• They have been linked to numerous health benefits including improved heart health, reduced inflammation, and enhanced immune function.
 
• Common dietary sources of flavonoids include apples, berries, onions, tea, and dark chocolate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Flavonoids:**

 
 
• Flavonols: Found in onions, kale, and broccoli.
 
• Flavan-3-ols: Present in tea, grapes, and cocoa.
 
• Anthocyanins: Provide red, purple, and blue colors to berries.
 
 
 
• **Antioxidant Properties:** Flavonoids help neutralize harmful free radicals in the body, reducing oxidative stress and preventing cell damage.
 
• **Anti-Inflammatory Effects:** These compounds can inhibit the production of pro-inflammatory molecules, thus aiding in the reduction of inflammation.
 
• **Cardiovascular Health:** Regular consumption of flavonoid-rich foods is associated with lower blood pressure, improved cholesterol levels, and reduced risk of heart disease.
 
• **Potential Cancer Prevention:** Some studies suggest that flavonoids may help in protecting against certain types of cancer by inhibiting tumor growth and promoting apoptosis in cancer cells.

questions.question: ______ are the oldest living tree species on Earth.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bristlecone pines**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• **Bristlecone pines are the oldest non-clonal species on the planet.**
 
• These strange trees are** shaped by the wind, snow, and rain **has survived for thousands of years.
 
• Their ability to survive these harsh environments and adverse growing conditions is exactly their secret to great longevity.
 
• Bristlecone pines in** Great Basin National Park grow** in isolated groves just below the tree line. 
 
• The Great Basin Bristlecone Pines are an extremely rare species found only in **California, Nevada, and Utah.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Redwood **is a subfamily of coniferous trees within the family Cupressaceae.

 
 
• It includes the **largest and tallest trees** in the world.
 
• It is also known as **Sequoia sempervirens**.
 
• The native habitat of Redwood trees is only on the western slopes of the Sierra Nevada range of California.

questions.question: Chili peppers produce a burning sensation in any tissue with which they come into contact. What is the compound responsible for this?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Capsaicin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Capsaicin** is the primary compound responsible for the burning sensation experienced when consuming chili peppers or when it comes into contact with tissue.
 
• It binds to a specific pain receptor known as **TRPV1 (Transient Receptor Potential Vanilloid 1)**, which is responsible for detecting heat and physical abrasion.
 
• The activation of TRPV1 by capsaicin tricks the brain into perceiving heat or burning, even though no actual thermal burn occurs.
 
• This compound is found in the highest concentration in the **placental tissue** of chili peppers, which surrounds the seeds.
 
• Capsaicin is insoluble in water but can be dissolved in fats and oils, making dairy products like milk effective at neutralizing its effects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Capsaicin's Uses:**

 
 
• Capsaicin is used in **topical creams and patches** to relieve pain from conditions like arthritis, muscle soreness, and nerve pain.
 
• Capsaicin is also used as an ingredient in **pepper sprays**, which are used for self-defense and crowd control.
 
• Studies suggest that capsaicin may have **metabolic benefits**, such as aiding weight loss by increasing metabolism.
 
• Capsaicin has anti-inflammatory properties and is being studied for its potential role in pain management therapies.
 
 
 
• **Other Compounds in Chili Peppers:**
 
 
• **Formic Acid:** Found in ant venom and some plants, formic acid causes irritation but is not responsible for the burning sensation of chili peppers.
 
• **Acetic Acid:** Found in vinegar, it provides a sour taste and is unrelated to the spiciness of chili peppers.
 
• **Lycopene:** A red pigment found in tomatoes and other red fruits, lycopene is an antioxidant but does not cause a burning sensation.
 
 
 
• **Scoville Heat Units (SHU):**
 
 
• The heat of chili peppers is measured in **Scoville Heat Units (SHU)**, which quantify the concentration of capsaicinoids.
 
• For example, bell peppers have 0 SHU, jalapeños range from 2,500 to 8,000 SHU, and the Carolina Reaper, one of the hottest peppers, measures over 2,200,000 SHU.
 
 
 
• **Health Benefits of Chili Peppers:**
 
 
• Chili peppers are rich in **vitamins A, C, and E**, as well as antioxidants that help combat inflammation and free radical damage.
 
• Consuming capsaicin in moderation may improve cardiovascular health and aid in digestion.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• Capsaicin does not cause tissue damage, even though it may feel like a burn; the sensation is temporary and caused by the activation of nerve receptors.
 
• Capsaicin-rich chili peppers have been used in traditional medicine for thousands of years to treat various ailments, from pain relief to digestive issues.
 
• Capsaicin has also been studied for its potential role in cancer treatment, as it may target and kill certain cancer cells without harming normal cells.

questions.question: Which of the following is a complex substance that provides structural strength to plants?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Cellulose.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cellulose is a fibrous carbohydrate found in all plants.**
 
• It is the structural component of plant cell walls.
 
• They are both made from the same monomer** (+) - glucose** and have the same glucose-based repeat units.
 
• In starch, all the glucose repeat units are oriented in the same direction. But in cellulose, each successive glucose unit is rotated 180 degrees around the axis of the polymer backbone chain, relative to the last repeat unit.
 
• Starch is practically useless as a material to make things, but cellulose is strong enough to make fibres, and hence rope, clothing and paper products.
 
• Cellulose doesn't dissolve in water the way starch does and certainly doesn't break down as easily.
 
• Cellulose is a polysaccharide (made up from sugar units) polymer.
 
• **The monosaccharide unit of the cellulose is Glucose.**
 
• The cell wall in the plant cells is made up of cellulose.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Xylem:**

 
 
• It is one of the important tissues of the vascular system of plants. The main activity of this tissue is to transport minerals and water from roots and carry them to other parts of the plants. It has two separate chambers tracheids and vessels for transporting minerals and water.
 
 
 
• **Phloem:**
 
 
• It is as important as the xylem tissues for the vascular system of plants. The main activity of this tissue is to transport nutrients and food from leaves to other growing parts of plants.
 
 
 
• **Cytoplasm:**
 
 
• Cytoplasm is a thick solution that fills each cell and is enclosed by the cell membrane.
 
• It is mainly composed of water, salts, and proteins. In eukaryotic cells, the cytoplasm includes all of the material inside the cell and outside of the nucleus.

questions.question: Tiny pores present on the surface of leaves are known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**stomata**__.

__
 
• **Tiny pores present on the surface of leaves are known as stomata**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Stomata:**

 
 
• Stomata are small pores present in the epidermis of leaves, stems and other plant parts.
 
• The stomata are surrounded by two guard cells.
 
• This allows gases such as carbon dioxide, water vapor and oxygen to diffuse into and out of the plant's internal tissues.
 
• It occurs mostly in vascular plants.
 
• The inner wall of the guard cell is thicker than the outer wall.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nucleus**

 
 
• It was discovered by **Robert Brown**.
 
• The nucleus is **rich in protein** and **RNA**.
 
• **Chromatin **is the controlling **center of a cell.**
 
 
 
• **Mitochondria:**
 
 
• It is a **semi-autonomous organelle** and called the **powerhouse **of the cell because in it stepwise oxidation of fuel occurs which results in a release of chemical energy.
 
• This **energy is stored in the form of ATP.**
 
 
 
• The **cytoplasm **is the fluid found **outside the nuclear membrane.**
